# FDGA064

> DO NOT have more than one public type in a source file, unless they differ only in the number of generic parameters or one is nested in the other.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section A.4 File Organization.

This is a coding style convention. The book treats the appendix A conventions as suggestions, so you can override it.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

planned-analyzer: more than one public type in a file.

## From the book

Multiple internal types in one file are allowed, though there is a preference for “one (top-level) type per file.”
